title: Eilidh nic Leòid opens the Ceann mhòr assize
summary: In the heat of an t-Iuchar, with the windows of the old magistrate's house propped open against the fish-yard smell, Eilidh nic Leòid tells the crowded room that she will hear all nineteen causes on the list to their own ends, in their own order, whatever the likeness of one paper to the next, and whatever the weather asks of everyone waiting on the bench.

title: The Dunlop title read to its end
summary: Eilidh nic Leòid reads a human grant brown at its folds, and a receipt for seed corn the family thought to bring unasked, and finds as she found seven years before at Seann Bhral: the ground is the Crown's, the working of it the Dunlops', on the same terms as before and no excusal from any due to come.

title: Fifteen suits found for the Crown at Ceann mhòr
summary: Cause after cause of the seventeen brought on human titles is decided in the words of the Leòid ruling, the ground passing to the Crown and the working of it staying with the family that holds it, until the room has learned, before the week is out, to stop guessing at an ending it already knows.

title: A custodian's countersign found on the Coombe title
summary: In the margin of a Tuathaich family's human grant, Eilidh nic Leòid finds the pressed mark of an old land-keeping custodian, witness to the transfer in the humans' own time, and rules that a grant allowed also by an office of the island's own older law stands on ground the crossing never touched.

title: The Coombes and the Pettifers found for the holders
summary: Two of the seventeen suits at Ceann mhòr, each carrying a custodian's old countersign on its title, are found whole for the families that hold them, the only two of the assize's nineteen causes decided against the Crown that summer.

title: Walter Hale heard as a witness at Ceann mhòr
summary: Having no standing to plead, Walter Hale is called instead to the bench as a witness, and shows Eilidh nic Leòid the Moot's own minute of a family's land divided by agreement and set down in writing years before, which the court accepts over the memory of the parties themselves.

title: The Moot's minute-books credited by a Crown bench
summary: Eilidh nic Leòid rules that a record kept by a body the Crown does not recognise is no less a fact for the hand that wrote it holding no seal, the first time the Moot's own paper is taken as evidence before a circuit justice.

title: Hale and Eilidh nic Leòid speak at the Ceann mhòr inn
summary: Over supper Walter Hale asks Eilidh nic Leòid whether an exact law can also be a fair one; she tells him plainly that she made her ruling to be exact rather than kind, and that she knows whose convenience it was written to serve, a thing she has told no maor and no council chest.

title: Eilidh nic Leòid begins the gathered book
summary: Through the winter after the Ceann mhòr sitting, Eilidh nic Leòid sets down in one book the whole of her nine years' rulings on Tuathaich land, from the Seann Bhral ruling to the seventeen suits, so that a justice after her need not dig the council's own chests to learn what she already knows.

title: Eilidh nic Leòid sends for Uilleam mac Leòid
summary: Failing through am Màrt, Eilidh nic Leòid sends word north to her brother's son Uilleam, a young man who has ridden the northern circuit with her twice as a boy, asking him to take up the circuit she can no longer ride.

title: Eilidh nic Leòid dies at Cathair dhomhain
summary: Eilidh nic Leòid dies in her own house within sound of the harbour, her clerk Murchadh Clàrc beside her and the gathered book of her rulings finished but not yet bound on the table by the bed.

title: Leabhar nam Breith bound
summary: The council's own binder binds Eilidh nic Leòid's gathered rulings in plain calf under the name she chose for it herself, Leabhar nam Breith, and every circuit justice after her is given a copy to carry.

title: Uilleam mac Leòid named to the northern circuit
summary: Uilleam mac Leòid is named circuit justice of the north in his aunt's place, and rides for his first assize with Leabhar nam Breith strapped behind his clerk's saddle, as the satchel of blank record-books was once strapped behind his aunt's.

title: Eilidh nic Leòid at the Seann Bhral harbour wall
summary: Riding on from Àth leathan by the western road after the Ceann mhòr assize, Eilidh nic Leòid stands a while before the light fails at the harbour wall of Seann Bhral in the west, where she gave the Leòid ruling seven years before, and says nothing of it to Murchadh Clàrc.
